report.interpretation: Cycle time is the agreed metric: median days from report date to close date for closed Southeast claims, grouped by report month. I compared claims reported May–Jul 2026 with those reported Jan–Apr 2026. Aug–Sep 2026 reports are left out of the comparison because most of those claims are still open, which makes them look fast.
report.answer: The slowdown is real. Median time to close for Southeast claims rose from 28 days (reported Jan–Apr 2026) to 38 days (reported May–Jul 2026). It peaked at 40 days for July reports. The best-supported cause is lost adjuster capacity. Two of the six Southeast adjusters left in May (ADJ-016 on 1 May, ADJ-017 on 15 May), and they weren't replaced. The four remaining adjusters now handle about 25–27 new claims a month each, up from about 16, and 34–36 in Aug–Sep. The slowdown shows up in every state and nearly every cause of loss, which fits a capacity problem better than a problem with one cause, state or weather event. Claim volume rose only modestly in May–Jul (about 100 to 108 a month), so staffing, not demand, explains most of it. August and September report volumes are higher, which may add further strain.
report.answer_sql: SELECT strftime(date_trunc('month', report_date), '%Y-%m') AS report_month, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status='closed') AS closed_claims, median(date_diff('day', report_date, close_date)) FILTER (WHERE status='closed') AS median_days_to_close FROM claims WHERE region='Southeast' AND report_date BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-07-31' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

findings.claim: Median days to close rose from 28 to 38 for Southeast claims reported May–Jul 2026 versus Jan–Apr 2026. The monthly median was 31 in April, 34.5 in May, 37 in June and 40 in July.
findings.evidence_sql: SELECT case when report_date>='2026-05-01' then 'post_may' else 'jan_apr' end p, median(date_diff('day',report_date,close_date)) med_days, count(*) closed_claims FROM claims WHERE region='Southeast' AND status='closed' AND report_date BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-07-31' GROUP BY 1

findings.claim: Two of six Southeast adjusters left in May 2026, and claims per active adjuster jumped from about 16 to about 25–27 a month, then 34–36 in Aug–Sep. Claim volume itself rose only modestly through July.
findings.evidence_sql: SELECT strftime(date_trunc('month',report_date),'%Y-%m') m, count(*) claims, count(distinct adjuster_id) adjusters, round(count(*)*1.0/count(distinct adjuster_id),1) per_adj FROM claims WHERE region='Southeast' AND report_date>='2026-01-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

findings.claim: The slowdown is broad. All three states are slower (FL 31 to 37 days, GA 27 to 38, NC 27 to 38). Collision went from 23 to 31 days and water damage from 37 to 54. The remaining adjusters each slowed down too.
findings.evidence_sql: SELECT case when report_date>='2026-05-01' then 'post' else 'pre' end p, state, count(*) n, median(date_diff('day',report_date,close_date)) med FROM claims WHERE region='Southeast' AND report_date BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-07-31' AND status='closed' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,1

hypotheses.hypothesis: Adjuster departures and higher caseload per adjuster
hypotheses.evidence: Two adjusters left in May and the four who remain carry about 60% more claims each. Every remaining adjuster's median close time rose.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Weather event driving a surge of claims
hypotheses.evidence: The weather_events table has no FL, GA or NC events since March 2026. Claim volume in May–Jul rose only modestly.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Change in mix of causes or states
hypotheses.evidence: Median close times rose in all three states and in nearly all cause groups, so mix doesn't explain it.
No duplicate rows were found. Incomplete recent months bias toward faster times, not slower, and I excluded Aug–Sep. The rise is visible from May to Jul.

hypotheses.hypothesis: A specific repair shop or vendor
hypotheses.evidence: I didn't test shop-level effects. The slowdown is broad, including home claims that have no repair shop, so a single shop is unlikely to be the cause.

data_quality_issues.issue: Recent report months (Aug–Sep 2026) have many claims still open, and cycle time counts only closed claims.
data_quality_issues.impact: Aug (28 days) and Sep (9 days) look faster than they will end up. They don't show that the problem has gone away.

charts.title: Southeast median days to close by report month
charts.sql: SELECT strftime(date_trunc('month', report_date), '%Y-%m') AS report_month, median(date_diff('day', report_date, close_date)) AS median_days FROM claims WHERE region='Southeast' AND status='closed' AND report_date BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2026-07-31' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

proposed_actions.title: Review Southeast adjuster staffing and rebalance caseload
proposed_actions.reason: Two adjusters left in May and weren't replaced. Remaining adjusters handle about 34–36 new claims a month in Aug–Sep, so backlog and cycle times will likely keep rising.

open_questions: Were the departed adjusters' open claims reassigned evenly? The warehouse only shows the current adjuster, so I can't check this.
